cases.name: yaw_settled
cases.why: Subject and object already on their thirds and the eyeline on the upper third: every axis satisfied, so the command is zero and the rover stays put.

cases.name: yaw_right_of_target
cases.why: Framing midpoint at 0.70 against a target of 0.50: the content must move left, so the rover turns right and the left side drives harder.

cases.name: yaw_left_of_target
cases.why: The mirror image: midpoint at 0.30, so the rover turns left.

cases.name: yaw_saturated
cases.why: A huge bearing error must saturate at max_cmd rather than producing a command the bridge cannot deliver.

cases.name: yaw_no_object
cases.why: With no object resolved the yaw axis falls back to holding the subject alone on their third.

cases.name: yaw_deadband_inside
cases.why: Error just inside the 0.02 deadband: the axis is satisfied and must not hunt.

cases.name: yaw_deadband_outside
cases.why: The same error just outside the deadband, where the loop must act. The pair brackets the threshold.

cases.name: yaw_gyro_brakes_overshoot
cases.why: Framing correct but the rover still rotating at 25 deg/s: D-3's inner loop must command the opposite way to stop it. This is the case vision alone cannot handle.

cases.name: yaw_gyro_already_turning_the_right_way
cases.why: Turning toward the target already, so the inner loop's correction is small.

cases.name: yaw_gyro_sign_flipped
cases.why: The gyro reading inverted: the inner loop must fight, not run away. Guards the rate_z_sign calibration.

cases.name: dist_too_close
cases.why: shoulder_px 0.150 against a swept target of 0.120: the subject fills too much of the frame, so the rover backs off.

cases.name: dist_too_far
cases.why: The reverse: 0.095 against 0.120, so the rover closes in.

cases.name: dist_deadband
cases.why: Inside the 3% deadband, so the distance axis is silent even though the number is not exactly the target.

cases.name: dist_arms_raised
cases.why: P-4: the subject raises their arms, so the box grows a lot and shoulder_px does not move at all. The distance command must be identical to dist_settled - reading box height here would look like 40 cm of travel.

cases.name: dist_no_shoulder_measurement
cases.why: Both shoulders occluded, so shoulder_px is None. P-7: hold rather than guess a distance.

cases.name: tilt_eyeline_high
cases.why: Eyes at 0.28 against a target of 0.333: the subject sits too high, the content must move down, so the camera tilts up and the commanded angle increases.

cases.name: tilt_eyeline_low
cases.why: Eyes at 0.46 against the same 0.333 target: the subject sits too low, so the camera tilts down and the commanded angle decreases. The mirror of the case above.

cases.name: tilt_step_clamped
cases.why: A huge tilt error must be taken in one bounded step, not a single lurch across the whole range.

cases.name: tilt_builds_on_previous_command
cases.why: D-9: the correction is added to the LAST COMMANDED angle, not to a gravity-referenced absolute. That is what absorbs backlash and missed steps.

cases.name: tilt_at_mechanical_limit
cases.why: Already at the top of the tilt range: the command must clamp rather than wind up.

cases.name: tilt_falls_back_to_nose
cases.why: Eyes not visible but the nose is: the eyeline falls back one rung rather than giving up.

cases.name: tilt_no_face_at_all
cases.why: No eyes, no nose: the eyeline is estimated from the box, which is the last rung before holding.

cases.name: gate_subject_moved
cases.why: D-6: shoulder_px jumped but the background did not move, so the SUBJECT moved. Hold and re-plan - reacting here would chase a person who is walking.

cases.name: gate_rover_moved
cases.why: The same jump with the background shifting: the ROVER moved, so the measurement is real and the loop acts on it.

cases.name: gate_no_flow_measurement
cases.why: No flow measurement at all is not evidence the background was still, so the gate must not fire.

cases.name: gate_small_change_ignored
cases.why: A change below shoulder_jump is noise, not motion, and must not trip the gate either way.

cases.name: speed_limited_near_an_obstacle
cases.why: D-8: range under 1000 mm halves the speed limit. Warmed up past the ramp so the CAP is what differs from the case below, not the acceleration.

cases.name: speed_unlimited_in_the_open
cases.why: The same error with clear ground, for comparison with the case above. The duty here must be strictly larger.

cases.name: sweep_first_sample
cases.why: The sweep starts by backing away - the safe direction, since the far end of the leg is unknown.

cases.name: sweep_collecting
cases.why: Part-way through collection, still driving and logging (shoulder_px, ratio) pairs.

cases.name: sweep_solved_and_returning
cases.why: Collection finished and solved; the rover now drives back to the shoulder_px that satisfies the ratio.

cases.name: sweep_rechecking_holds_still
cases.why: D-8: a full stop before any measurement used for a final decision, so the recheck happens with the wheels stopped.

cases.name: sweep_fails_and_speaks_up
cases.why: The object scaled with the subject across the whole sweep, so the fitted curve is flat and no distance gives the requested ratio. This case catches the TRANSITION into failure, which is where the spoken line is produced.

cmd_out.say: I can't get that framing from here - the background is too far away.

cases.name: feasible_still_improving
cases.why: The gap between subject and object is opening as the rover drives, so stay quiet and keep going.

cases.name: infeasible_asks_the_subject_to_step
cases.why: D-7: the spacing has not improved over the whole window, so turning and driving cannot fix it. Propose the fix, in the subject's own left/right.

cmd_out.say: Could you step a metre to your right?

cases.name: ramp_from_standstill
cases.why: First tick of a big move: the normalised command is rate limited, but the duty that comes out still clears the bridge's dead band, so the logged command is what the wheels got.

cases.name: ramp_mid_move
cases.why: Four ticks into the same move, with the ramp part-way up.

cases.name: stop_is_immediate
cases.why: Deceleration is not rate limited: a satisfied loop stops on the tick, rather than ramping down through duties the bridge cannot turn.

cases.name: phase_idle_inhibits_motors
cases.why: CO-3: motors are inhibited in idle. The GoalSpec is locked before the first command that sets enable (G-1).

cases.name: phase_listen_inhibits_motors
cases.why: CO-3: motors are inhibited in listen. The GoalSpec is locked before the first command that sets enable (G-1).

cases.name: phase_parse_inhibits_motors
cases.why: CO-3: motors are inhibited in parse. The GoalSpec is locked before the first command that sets enable (G-1).

cases.name: phase_confirm_inhibits_motors
cases.why: CO-3: motors are inhibited in confirm. The GoalSpec is locked before the first command that sets enable (G-1).

cases.name: goal_not_locked_inhibits_motors
cases.why: G-1 again, from the other side: even in the frame phase, an unlocked goal must not energise anything.

cases.name: phase_arm_tracks_tilt_only
cases.why: Armed but not yet framing: the tilt axis tracks so the commanded angle does not jump on entry, and the wheels stay still.

cases.name: phase_settle_holds_position
cases.why: PG-5: position is locked before coaching or capture.

cases.name: phase_capture_fires
cases.why: First frame of the capture burst: the capture flag goes up while the wheels stay stopped, so the shutter never fires during a manoeuvre.

cases.name: phase_capture_burst_exhausted
cases.why: After burst_frames, the capture flag drops so the phone is not asked for an endless stream of stills.

cases.name: phase_halted_stops
cases.why: CO-4: the subject is the only positional reference, so losing them stops the motors.

cases.name: phase_search_spins
cases.why: CO-4: a slow gyro-guided spin toward the last known bearing. Equal and opposite duty - the rover must never DRIVE while it cannot see the subject.

cases.name: phase_search_reverses_at_the_limit
cases.why: Past the +-60 degree cap the search turns back rather than spinning on forever.

cases.name: pose_point_large_error
cases.why: CO-1: more than 20 degrees out, so the cue is the blunt one. The limb is pinned so this case measures the ANGLE; limb selection has its own case below.

cmd_out.say: Raise your right arm a lot

cases.name: pose_point_medium_error
cases.why: CO-1: squarely in the 8-20 degree band, where the cue is a nudge rather than a correction.

cases.name: pose_point_in_tolerance
cases.why: Inside +-3 degrees: no correction, and the hold countdown begins.

cases.name: pose_point_foreshortened
cases.why: PG-3: the forearm is far shorter than shoulder_px implies, so the angle is untrustworthy and the remedy is to turn side-on rather than any angle correction.

cmd_out.say: Turn side-on to me a little

cases.name: pose_limb_chosen_by_object_side
cases.why: G-4 and the mirror: the object is on the image-right, and the subject's LEFT wrist is the one at the larger image x, so the left arm is chosen.

cmd_out.say: Raise your left arm a lot

cases.name: pose_hold_goal
cases.why: PG-1: wrist to object centre, +-2% of frame width.

cases.name: pose_look_at_goal
cases.why: PG-1: the eyes-to-nose gaze proxy against the head-to-object direction, +-8 degrees.

cmd_out.say: Turn your head a lot to your left

cases.name: pose_template_arms_out
cases.why: PG-1's template row, measured as joint angles against the template and reporting the worse side.

cmd_out.say: Raise your left arm a lot

cases.name: pose_no_overlap
cases.why: PG-1: subject box against object box, tolerance exactly zero.

cases.name: pose_bias_absorbed_by_the_rover
cases.why: PG-4's rover-first policy: a small pose error in the FRAME phase biases the framing targets instead of asking the person to move. Driving shifts the object relative to the subject through parallax.

cases.name: pose_unmeasurable_keypoints
cases.why: P-7 end to end: the wrist is low-confidence, so there is no error, no cue and no guess.
